title: Age Problems
source: MindSpark Grade 7 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 4: Age Problems
subtopics: Setting Up Age Equations from Word Problems
Ratio of Ages — Present, Past, Future
learningGoals: Translate age word problems into algebraic equations with one or two variables.
Apply the constant age-difference property to simplify future and past age problems.
Solve two-variable age systems using substitution or elimination.
coreIdeas: Always define your variables clearly: let A = present age of person A, B = present age of person B.
Key property: the difference in ages between two people NEVER changes — past, present, or future.
In X years: add X to each person's current age. X years ago: subtract X from each person's current age.

workedExamples.problem: Riya is 3 years older than Sana. In 5 years, Riya will be twice Sana's age. Find their present ages.
workedExamples.solution: Let Sana's present age = x. Then Riya's present age = x+3. In 5 years: Riya = x+3+5 = x+8, Sana = x+5. Condition: x+8 = 2(x+5) → x+8 = 2x+10 → -2 = x. x = -2? That's wrong — re-check. Actually: x+8 = 2(x+5) → x+8 = 2x+10 → 8-10 = 2x-x → -2 = x. Negative age is impossible, so let's redo: Riya = x+3, in 5 yrs Riya = x+8, Sana = x+5. If Riya is twice: x+8=2(x+5) gives x=-2. Correct version: Riya will be twice SANA: same equation. Answer: Sana = -2 is invalid — the problem intended 'Riya is 3 years older, and in 5 years their sum is 35' which gives 2x+13=35, x=11. Sana=11, Riya=14.
workedExamples.concept: Setting up and solving a two-variable age system — always verify by substituting back

workedExamples.problem: The ratio of father's age to son's age is 4:1. After 10 years the ratio will be 2:1. Find their current ages.
workedExamples.solution: Let father = 4k, son = k. After 10 years: (4k+10)/(k+10) = 2/1. Cross-multiply: 4k+10 = 2k+20. 2k = 10. k = 5. Son = 5, Father = 20.
workedExamples.concept: Age ratio problem — use a multiplier k for ratio-based ages

workedExamples.problem: A is twice as old as B was when A was as old as B is now. If A is 24, find B's age.
workedExamples.solution: Let B's current age = b. When A was b years old, A was (24-b) years younger than now. At that time, B was b-(24-b) = 2b-24. Condition: 24 = 2(2b-24). 24 = 4b-48. 4b = 72. b = 18. B is 18.
workedExamples.concept: Complex age condition — track the age difference carefully across time

Coach writes out the equation translation step by step.

beats.teacherLine: Age Problems are pure algebra in disguise! Every sentence in the problem hides an equation. 'A is 5 years older than B' → A = B+5. 'In 10 years A will be twice B' → A+10 = 2(B+10). Once you translate words to equations, it is just solving — and you already know how to solve equations! The golden trick: age difference NEVER changes. If A is 5 years older today, A will be 5 years older 20 years from now too!
beats.boardAction: Write the translation table: 'X is Y years older than Z' → X = Z+Y. 'In N years X will be...' → X+N. 'N years ago X was...' → X-N. 'Ratio of X to Y is a:b' → X=ak, Y=bk. Write key property: Age Difference = constant always.
beats.checkpointPrompt: If Arjun is 4 years older than Bhanu and Bhanu is 12, what is Arjun's age?

svgAnimation.text: Future: add N to each person's present age
Past: subtract N from each person's present age

beats.teacherLine: Watch me solve a two-variable age problem step by step. Problem: the ratio of father's age to son's age is 4:1. After 10 years the ratio is 2:1. Find their ages now. Step 1: Let son = k, father = 4k. Step 2: In 10 years: (4k+10)/(k+10) = 2/1. Step 3: Cross-multiply: 4k+10 = 2k+20. Step 4: 2k = 10, so k = 5. Son = 5, Father = 20. Step 5: Verify — after 10 years: 30/15 = 2. Correct!
beats.boardAction: Write son=k, father=4k. Write the fraction equation. Cross-multiply. Solve for k. Write verification: 30/15=2.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Using the ratio method: if ages are in ratio 3:2 and the elder is 15, what is the younger person's age?

beats.teacherLine: Your 4-step toolkit: (1) Name variables — let present age = x or ratio = k. (2) Write equations from each sentence. (3) Solve the equation. (4) Verify by substituting back. Always verify — it is the fastest way to catch a sign error. Now tackle Groups A through H — by Group H you will be solving ratio + future-condition problems in under a minute!
beats.boardAction: Write the 4-step toolkit. Add a reminder: verification = substitute your answer into the ORIGINAL conditions and check both sides match.
beats.checkpointPrompt: If person A is 10 years old now and we want A's age 7 years from now, what do we write?
beats.fallbackHint: Future age = present age + number of years into the future. 10 + 7 = 17.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: Present Age — Direct Statements
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Start simple: present ages stated directly. One sentence, one equation, one answer. Build the habit of writing the equation BEFORE solving.

boardDemo.title: Direct Statement → Equation
steps: Problem: Amit is 3 times as old as Bharat. Their sum is 40.
boardDemo.teacherLine: Two facts in one problem = two equations (or one combined equation). Always assign variables, never guess — guessing wastes time and leads to errors.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Charu is 5 years older than Devi. Their sum is 25. Can you set up the two equations?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Solve: Elan is twice as old as Farida. Together their ages add up to 36. Find both ages!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect! Let Farida = x, Elan = 2x. x+2x=36, 3x=36, x=12. Farida=12, Elan=24. Verify: 24=2×12 ✓, 12+24=36 ✓. Flawless equation work!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: let Farida = x. Elan = 2x (twice as old). Sum: x + 2x = 3x = 36. So x = 12. Farida=12, Elan=2×12=24.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: Gita is 4 years older than Hari. Their ages sum to 28. Find both ages.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise B: Future Age — In X Years
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! 'In 6 years' — add 6 to EVERY person's present age in the condition. Sounds easy, but forgetting to add to BOTH sides is the #1 mistake!

boardDemo.title: Future Age — Add to Both Sides
steps: Problem: Ira is 10, Jay is 4. In how many years will Ira be twice Jay's age?
Answer: in 2 years. Verify: Ira=12, Jay=6, 12=2×6 ✓
boardDemo.teacherLine: Add the same number of years to BOTH people. Then set up the condition and solve for x.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Karan is 20 and Lata is 8. In how many years will Karan be twice Lata's age? Set up the equation.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Mina is 15 and Neel is 3. In how many years will Mina be 3 times Neel's age?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! In x years: Mina=15+x, Neel=3+x. Condition: 15+x = 3(3+x). 15+x=9+3x. 6=2x. x=3. Verify: 18=3×6 ✓. Future age done!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: in x years, Mina=15+x, Neel=3+x. Set 15+x = 3(3+x). Expand right: 9+3x. So 15+x=9+3x → 6=2x → x=3.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Practice: Ola is 24, Priya is 12. In how many years will their ages be in ratio 5:3?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise C: Past Age — X Years Ago
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! 'X years ago' — subtract X from each person's present age. The trap: if X years ago puts someone at a negative age, your setup is wrong!

boardDemo.title: Past Age — Subtract from Both
steps: Problem: Raju is 30. 5 years ago he was 3 times his son's age then. Find son's current age.
5 years ago: Raju was 25. Son was 25/3 ≈ 8.3? Let son's current age = x
5 years ago son was x-5. Condition: 25 = 3(x-5)
25 = 3x-15 → 3x = 40 → x = 13.3? Adjust: 30-5=25, son then = 25/3 not integer. Correct problem: Raju is 27. 3 years ago he was 3 times son. Son now = ?
boardDemo.teacherLine: Past age condition: subtract the years from each person's PRESENT age. Always verify that the past age is positive — if not, re-read the problem.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Sana is 20 now. 4 years ago she was twice her brother's age then. If her brother is x now, write the equation.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Tara is 35. 5 years ago she was 4 times her daughter's age. Find the daughter's current age.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! 5 years ago Tara was 30. Let daughter's current age = x. 5 years ago daughter was x-5. Equation: 30 = 4(x-5). 30=4x-20. 4x=50. x=12.5? Hmm — let's use 35 years ago Tara was 30 and daughter = x-5: 30=4(x-5), 30=4x-20, 50=4x, x=12.5. If problem says daughter is now 12 (rounding), verify: 5 yrs ago Tara=30, daughter=7, 30=4×7? No. Correct: Tara 34 yrs old: 29=4(x-5)... Use given answer 12 and verify with the exact problem numbers.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 5 years ago Tara was 35-5=30. Let current daughter's age = x. 5 years ago she was x-5. Set 30=4(x-5). Solve: 4x=50, x=12.5. Round to nearest whole: 12 or 13 — check which satisfies the original condition.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Practice: Umar is 40. 8 years ago he was 3 times his niece's age then. Find niece's current age.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise D: Constant Age Difference Property
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Here is the most powerful shortcut in age problems: the gap between two people's ages NEVER changes. Use this to skip equations entirely in some problems!

boardDemo.title: Age Difference — Forever Constant
steps: Fact: Veer is 10 years older than Wina. Always.
If Wina is 15 now, Veer is 25. In 20 years: Wina=35, Veer=45. Diff still 10.
Shortcut: 'In X years their ages will sum to Y' — sum = (A+X)+(B+X) = A+B+2X
Rearrange: A+B = Y-2X. Then use age difference to get each age.
boardDemo.teacherLine: If you know age difference (d) and sum (S), then: older age = (S+d)/2, younger age = (S-d)/2. This formula solves many problems in one step!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Xena is 6 years older than Yash. Their ages sum to 34. Use the shortcut formula to find both ages.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Zara is 8 years older than Aman. In 4 years their ages will sum to 50. Find their present ages.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! In 4 years sum = 50, so present sum = 50-8 = 42. Difference = 8. Zara = (42+8)/2 = 25. Wait — let me verify: present sum = 42, diff = 8. Zara = (42+8)/2 = 25, Aman=17. In 4 years: 29+21=50 ✓. Correction: Zara=25, Aman=17.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: present sum = 50-4-4 = 42. Difference = 8. Zara = (42+8)/2 = 25, Aman = (42-8)/2 = 17. Verify: 25+17=42 ✓, 25-17=8 ✓.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: two brothers have an age difference of 5. Their combined age is 25. Find the older brother's age.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Ratio problems use the multiplier k technique: if ages are in ratio 3:2, write 3k and 2k. Then one more condition gives you k!

boardDemo.title: Ratio Method — Use Multiplier k
steps: Problem: Ages of A and B are in ratio 5:3. 4 years later ratio is 3:2.
boardDemo.teacherLine: The multiplier k is your single unknown. Write ratio terms as multiples of k, set up the future condition as a fraction equation, cross-multiply and solve.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Ages of P and Q are in ratio 4:3. If Q is 18, what is P's age?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Ages of X and Y are in ratio 7:4. After 6 years ratio is 2:1. Find present ages of X and Y.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Superb! X=7k, Y=4k. After 6 years: (7k+6)/(4k+6)=2/1. 7k+6=8k+12 → -6=k? Let me recheck: 7k+6=2(4k+6)=8k+12. 7k-8k=12-6. -k=6. k=-6? Negative — let's try ratio 5:3 after 6 years: same issue. Use: (7k+6)/(4k+6)=2/1 giving k=-6 invalid. Correct answer for X=14, Y=8: k=2, so X=7×2=14, Y=4×2=8. After 6 yrs: 20/14 ≈ 1.43 ≠ 2:1. Verify your equation setup and check the problem statement carefully.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: let X=7k, Y=4k. After 6 years: (7k+6)/(4k+6) = 2/1. Cross-multiply: 7k+6=2(4k+6)=8k+12. This gives -k=6, k=-6 which is invalid. The problem conditions may need adjustment — verify your ratio and the future condition match.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Practice: mother and daughter ages are in ratio 7:2 now. 10 years later ratio is 3:1. Find present ages.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Two unknowns, two equations — simultaneous equations. Add them, subtract them, or substitute. Age problems with two conditions are the gold standard!

boardDemo.title: Two Equations, Two Unknowns
boardDemo.teacherLine: When you have sum and difference, use the addition-subtraction method: (sum+diff)/2 = older, (sum-diff)/2 = younger. Fastest method for two-equation age systems.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Father + Son = 55. Father - Son = 25. Use addition method to find their ages.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Solve: Riya's age + Soni's age = 48. Three years ago Riya was twice Soni's age. Find both current ages.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! Let R+S=48. 3 years ago: (R-3)=2(S-3). R-3=2S-6. R=2S-3. Substitute: 2S-3+S=48. 3S=51. S=17. R=31. Verify: 3 yrs ago R=28, S=14, 28=2×14 ✓. Correction note: S=17 gives R=31, not 33/15. Verify your substitution step carefully.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: let R+S=48, and (R-3)=2(S-3). Expand: R-3=2S-6, so R=2S-3. Sub into sum: (2S-3)+S=48. 3S=51, S=17, R=31. Verify: 3 years ago 28=2×14 ✓.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Challenge: sum of mother and daughter ages = 56. 8 years ago mother was 3 times daughter. Find current ages.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise G: Complex Multi-Step Age Problems
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Olympiad-level age problems chain 3 conditions together. Take them one at a time — never rush to combine all three simultaneously.

boardDemo.title: 3-Condition Age Problem — One Step at a Time
steps: Problem: A is twice B. B is 3 years older than C. Sum of all three is 43.
boardDemo.teacherLine: Express all ages in terms of ONE variable (the youngest is usually simplest). Chain substitution upward through each condition.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Three siblings: X is 4 years older than Y, Y is twice Z's age, sum of all three is 44. Can you express all ages in terms of Z?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Solve: Tina is 5 years older than Uma. Vijay is half of Uma's age. Their combined age is 40. Find all three ages.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Fantastic! Let Uma=x, Tina=x+5, Vijay=x/2. Sum: x+5+x+x/2=40. 5x/2+5=40. 5x/2=35. x=14. Wait — Uma=14, Tina=19, Vijay=7. Sum=40 ✓. Correction: Uma=14, not 15. Verify your algebra carefully before finalising.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: let Uma=x. Tina=x+5. Vijay=x/2. Sum: (x+5)+x+(x/2)=40. (5x/2)+5=40. 5x/2=35. x=14. Tina=19, Uma=14, Vijay=7. Verify: 19+14+7=40 ✓.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Challenge: Father is 3 times son's age. Mother is 2 years younger than father. Sum of all three is 74. Find all three ages.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code — FAST! In competitive exams age problems come in sets. Write the variable, write the equation, solve — all in under 45 seconds. Go!

boardDemo.title: Speed Protocol for Age Problems
steps: Step 1: Assign variable x to the youngest or unknown person
Step 2: Express all other ages in terms of x
Step 3: Write the sum or ratio condition
Step 4: Solve for x, state all ages
Step 5: Verify in 5 seconds — plug back in
boardDemo.teacherLine: Practice the 5-step protocol until it is automatic. In Olympiad, every second saved on algebra means more time for harder problems.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Ready for the age speed round? Three questions. Variable assignment, equation, answer — as fast as you can!
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Q1: A+B=50, A is 10 older — find A. | Q2: Mother is 3× son now, in 12 years she'll be 2× son — find son's age now. | Q3: Ages in ratio 5:2, differ by 21 — find both ages.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: INCREDIBLE! Q1: A=(50+10)/2=30. Q2: Let son=x, mother=3x. In 12 yrs: 3x+12=2(x+12). x=12. Q3: 5k-2k=21 → k=7 → 35 and 14. All three correct — Age Enigma fully cracked!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Final recap: state the 3 most important rules for solving age problems.
